quotes.text: A forward migration (to shift nsMsgKeys in existing databases to a separate UID field) needs to land along with the main change.
All ambiguous uses of message keys in the IMAP code should be audited to determine if they really are message keys, or if they're being used as a UID.

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: ADR0002 is marked Approved and records the decision to store IMAP server UID separately while the database manages a stable messageKey. It calls for auditing ambiguous UID/key uses, avoiding nsMsgKey for protocol UIDs, and landing forward migration with the main change. It describes redownload/Repair Folder as a possible downgrade route and treats advance compatibility support as a policy option. These are accepted architecture-document statements, not proof the migration is implemented, a measured recovery result, or authorization to edit user instructions. Current conversion bodies are checked separately. Required review has a removed human body, so this source-only note gives no full-audit credit.
title: ADR0002 records approved UID separation and a coordinated migration plan
